# Deleveraging

The downswing of the debt cycle. There are four ways for debt to fall relative to income: austerity, default and restructuring, transfers from those who have to those who owe, and money creation.

## Ugly and less ugly

When austerity and default dominate, incomes fall faster than debt and the burden rises even as people pay down what they owe. When money creation offsets the contraction, the ratio falls without a collapse in incomes, at the cost of a weaker currency.

The definition I am using is in [[Long debt cycle#^debt-def]]. For the trigger see [[Minsky moment#The moment]], and for the staging ![[Minsky moment#Three stages]].
